reference_sql:
SELECT isoyear(order_ts) AS iso_year,
       week(order_ts) AS iso_week,
       COUNT(*) AS orders
FROM orders
WHERE order_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2024-12-16 00:00:00'
  AND order_ts < TIMESTAMP '2025-01-13 00:00:00'
GROUP BY 1, 2
alternatives: SELECT EXTRACT(isoyear FROM order_ts) AS iso_year, EXTRACT(week FROM order_ts) AS iso_week, COUNT(*) AS orders FROM orders WHERE order_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2024-12-16 00:00:00' AND order_ts < TIMESTAMP '2025-01-13 00:00:00' GROUP BY 1, 2

SELECT isoyear(date_trunc('week', order_ts)) AS iso_year, week(date_trunc('week', order_ts)) AS iso_week, COUNT(*) AS orders FROM orders WHERE order_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2024-12-16 00:00:00' AND order_ts < TIMESTAMP '2025-01-13 00:00:00' GROUP BY date_trunc('week', order_ts)

other_way.sql: SELECT isoyear(date_trunc('week', order_ts)) AS iso_year, week(date_trunc('week', order_ts)) AS iso_week, COUNT(*) AS orders FROM orders WHERE order_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2024-12-16 00:00:00' AND order_ts < TIMESTAMP '2025-01-13 00:00:00' GROUP BY date_trunc('week', order_ts)
other_way.tradeoff: Grouping by the Monday from date_trunc('week', ...) gives the same ISO weeks, and you read the labels off that Monday.
